---
name: run-recorder
description: After each agent run in this repo, makes runs/<session>-<run>.json from the session log. It groups the tool uses into steps and writes why for each step, use and file. The timeline of the page shows it as an Agent run block.
tools: Bash, Read, Write
---

You record one agent run. A run is one request to the agent: from a message (a person, the coordinator, a notification) to the next one.

1. Get the raw data:
   `node scripts/run-log.js <transcript.jsonl> --repo . --from <commit before the run> --to <commit after the run> --version <state version of the release> [--run N]`
   - The transcript is the session log: `~/.claude/projects/<project folder>/<session id>.jsonl`. Without `--run`, the script uses the last run.
   - The raw data has: `session`, `run`, `started`, `ended`, `started_by`, `context`, `uses`, `events` (each tool use, in order, with the `context` and `cached` tokens of its request, and the `files` it read or changed) and `files`.
   - The script finds files that the tools read or wrote, and files that shell commands changed (a python script that writes a file, sed -i, a redirect, rm). git finds the files of the repo that changed. If the events show a change that the script did not find, add it.
2. Read the raw data. Then write `runs/<session>-<run>.json` with these fields. Use ASD-STE100: short sentences, one instruction or fact in each sentence.
   - All the raw fields, but not `events` (put what is important into the steps).
   - `title`: the goal of the run in 3 to 8 words.
   - `started_by`: keep `session` and `run` (who, words, at) and add `why` to each: why the session started, and what the run had to do. Add `workflow`, `subagents` and `skills`: for each one that started in this run, `{name, why}` (what started it and why). Use `[]` or `null` when there is none.
   - `steps`: 3 to 12 steps, in order. Each step: `{title, lane, from, to, items, why, context_tokens, cached_tokens, files}`.
     - `title`: what the step did, for example "Find how the timeline draws blocks".
     - `lane`: `main`, or the name of the subagent that did the step. You are a subagent too: add your own step ("Record the run") in the lane `run-recorder`.
     - `items`: 2 to 8 short lines, for example "read index.html (sense, call)" or "create scripts/run-log.js". Each item is `{text, kind}`. kind is one of read, search, create, edit, delete, run, test, mcp, skill, subagent, workflow, publish.
     - `why`: one or two sentences: why the agent did this step.
     - `context_tokens` and `cached_tokens`: the context at the end of the step (from the events and `context`).
     - `files`: the files of the step: `{path, action}` for each file in the `files` of its events. action: read, created (written for the first time in the run), updated (edited, or written again) or deleted. A repo file that git says changed, but no event shows, goes into the step that made it (for example the step that ran the generator). The timeline shows them as a tree when you click the step.
   - `uses`: `{mcp, skills, subagents, workflows}`. Each is a list with one `{name, count, why}` for each MCP tool, skill, subagent or workflow.
   - `files`: each file from the raw data: `{path, action, tokens, cached, why}`. action is read, created, updated or deleted (git wins over the tools). tokens is the size that went into the context (about). cached is true when the file is in the cached part of the context at the end. why: one sentence.
3. Do not put secrets, tokens or passwords into the file. Do not copy the content of files: only paths and sizes.
4. Give the path of the file. The release (CLAUDE.md, Releases) puts the files of main into the state, so the run is in `agents.agent-oss.files.runs`.

# Agent OS

The page runs from its state. `index.html` is only a runtime: it loads the newest saved version of the state, then renders `extension.views.index-view`, and everything after that comes from the state: the page html and styles (in index-view `html`) and the state editor (the code of state-view's functions).

- `state.json`: the starting state (version 1 when the page has no history yet). Saved versions may hold `//` and `/* */` comments; Save repairs common JSON slips first (`autofix` in `state-core.js`). Cmd+S / Ctrl+S saves from anywhere on the page.
- Views (`extension.views.*`): a view's `html` starts with one root element whose id is the view's name (`<header id="header-view">`); render puts it in place of the empty element with that id in the parent view's html. `html` is a template: `${...}` sees the view's `ui-data` as `d`, `e()` escapes text), then `ui-data` (everything the view shows, e.g. state-view's `current_state_version`), `functions`.
- Functions (`extension.functions.*` and a view's `local.*`): `input`, `output`, `imports` (where each import line of the code comes from: `"index.html"` for the runtime's `os` and `ctx`, script URLs, full module source, or a state path to source or URLs kept once; stylesheets are blocked on claude.ai so styles go inline), `tests`, `expected-state-change`, `docs`, `pseudo` (the code step by step in short lines with keywords SET/READ/IF/ELSE/FOR EACH/CALL/DRAW/WATCH/WAIT/RETURN/THROW, 2 spaces per level; kept in the generator's `gen/pseudo.py`, change it when the code changes), `performance` (`last`/`min`/`max`/`count` in ms), `code`, `calls`. With `code`, `code` is a module as it looks in code: import lines (`import os from 'os';`, each a key of `imports`), then `async function name({ params }) { ... }`, called with `input` (the parameters, e.g. `{ "view_path": ... }`) (older versions have no import lines and get `ctx`, `os` and `imports`; older still, a bare body); with no code, the declared `calls` run in order. `output`, `performance`, each call's `output` and each test's `result` and `errors` are filled in after every run. `errors` lists a throw and anything `expected-state-change` did not allow: `{path: "changes" | "toggles" | "input" | "same" | "may change" | value}`, `"*"` allows any change. Changes made by nested calls count for them, not for the caller, so a function that changes nothing itself has `{}`.
- A view can watch the state with `os.watch(view, fn)`: that function runs after each top-level call (state-view's `local.refresh` redraws its bar and syncs the editor this way). `os.refs` holds what can't live in the state (the editor instance, unsaved text).
- Buttons in a view's html call functions with `data-call="local.x"` (and `data-input` as JSON).
- Tests: `{ "before": {call: input}, "input": ..., "expect": { "output": {...}, "output-has": [...], "dom": [...], "dom-absent": [...], "state": {path: value}, "state-changed": [paths] } }`. The state is checked after the run.
- `state-core.js`: paths, templates, diffs, the changes view, commits, history steps, test checks and the call tracker.
- `tests/`: `node --test tests/*.test.js` (set `CM_DIR` to a local codemirror@5.65.16 package to run the page test offline).
- On claude.ai the page stores `commits/c000001`… (`n`, `parent`, `at`, `state`, `summary`, `paths`, and `source` for a release; a database document holds at most 256 KB, so a bigger version has `stateGz`, its state gzipped in base64, instead of `state`; the runtime unpacks it when it reads) and `calls/<session>` (each call: `name`, `input`, `output`, `ok`, `error`, `ms`, `related` with `fn`, `parent`, `stateChanges`, `performance`).

- `output` is what the function returned (JSON, runtime fields stripped); nothing returned is `{}`.
- Docs: `agents.agent-oss.files.docs` (one string per file, ASD-STE100), shown by the header's Docs button in `extension.views.docs-view`.
- The state view's viewer opens any long text (`"..."`; the pointer on it shows its start). For html, `os.preview(frame, state, viewPath, id)` runs that view in the frame with a copy of the state (the runtime and state-core run in the frame's window): its buttons work, nothing is saved, and the frame posts the view's `ui-data` and the changes after each action.
- Timeline (`extension.views.timeline-view`, rendered by state-view `local.init`; shown when state-view `ui-data.timeline_open`, the Timeline button at the left of the state view's bar): drawn from `os.calls` (the runtime's call records for this page load: `input.via` = start / click / watch / test, `related.parent` = the call it ran inside, `related.stateChanges` = what that function itself changed, before and after) and `os.started`. Not kept in the state, so drawing it never changes the state. It sits above the header: a row of blocks (`os.refs['timeline-view'].steps`; the last agent run is `.pin-left` and the newest block `.pin-right`, sticky), replay (`ui-data.playing` / `ui-data.selected`; null = the last agent run), and state-view `ui-data.track_state` (Track state: the calls of the timeline, the state view and the record button are blocks only when on). There is no step-view: the state view shows the chosen block (`os.refs['timeline-view'].current`, `number`, `versionOf`): it goes to the block's version (`os.refs['state-view'].block` / `onBlock`; Older/Newer, a draft and Save leave the block), names it in `#sv-block`, and draws in its pane `#tl-detail` Details (`drawDetails`, state-view `ui-data.details`), Changes (`drawChanges(box, kind)` for the block, `drawPair(box, kind, pairFrom(before, after, from, head))` for a version) or one kind of the state as a tree (`kindView`). Changes all = the state cut down to the changes (`stateBox`; long strings as `"..."`, `longTexts`/`preview`; the hover preview `showTip(el, text, path, before)` is a CodeMirror in the mode of the path, with the line diff of an updated text) and a table; the filter text is state-view `ui-data.filter`; a kind (state-view `filter_kind`: all / files / views / functions / network / environment) shows in `kindView` (tree of all items of that kind on the left, tabs File|View|Function|Request|Value, Pseudo code for a function (`pseudoView`), and Changes on the right; chosen item and tab in `os.refs['timeline-view'].pick`); a file shows in `fileView(name, text)` by its kind (`fileKind`): md as a page (`mdPane`, the state view's md look and `md_theme`, contents), json as a tree (`jsonPane`), code with an outline (`outlineOf`) and find/wrap/copy (`codePane`); md and json have a Source mode (`os.refs['timeline-view'].fileMode`); md Read has the six `.md-theme` buttons, which call state-view `local.set-md-theme`; Full screen (`.fv-full`, `os.refs['timeline-view'].fileFull`, Escape exits); the "..." viewer (`preview`) uses it too. Each call row in Details lists what it changed. `ui-data.show_blocks` hides the row; `ui-data.flows` = saved flows `{name, steps: [block names]}` played by `local.play-flow` (`os.refs['timeline-view'].flow`), listed when `ui-data.flows_open`.
- `network` and `environment` (top of the state): the runtime fills them (`sense()` in index.html) when each call starts and ends, so a call's `stateChanges` show what it loaded and what changed around the page; `expected-state-change` leaves them out. `network.<group>.<name>`: groups html, scripts, claude.ai (`/_runtime/` scripts of the artifact page, keyed without their hash), api (database calls), state, file code, packages, styles, other; measured `url`, `start`, `ms`, `size`, `count`, `parallel`; written by the owner: `used_for`, `expected` (true = the state lists this request; a new one gets false). `environment`: also document, window, event listeners, timers, observers, connections (index.html wraps addEventListener/removeEventListener, setTimeout/setInterval/requestAnimationFrame, the observers' observe/disconnect, WebSocket/EventSource/BroadcastChannel at the top of the runtime; `by` = the newest running call, `running`), devices, permissions (asked in `askLater()`); browser (fixed values are read once: `fixedInfo()`), browser data (storages, with `claude.ai database` from `claudeDb()`), browser api, subscriptions, background services, other. Timeline block 1 (Network) shows both, with the values of the version the page loaded.
- Agent runs: `runs/<session>-<run>.json` (in the state at `agents.agent-oss.files.runs`, as text). `scripts/run-log.js <transcript.jsonl> [--run N] [--repo . --from REV --to REV] [--version N]` prints the raw data of a run from the Claude Code session log (`~/.claude/projects/<folder>/<session>.jsonl`): `started_by`, `context` (tokens: input + cache read + cache write; cached = cache read), `uses` (mcp, skills, subagents, workflows), `events` (each tool use), `files` (read / created / updated / deleted; git wins). The `run-recorder` subagent (`.claude/agents/run-recorder.md`) turns it into the run file: no `events`, plus `title`, `steps` (`{title, lane, from, to, items, why, context_tokens, cached_tokens, files: [{path, action}]}`), and `why` on each use and file. No secrets, no file contents. The timeline (`runsOf`, `runStep`, `runDetails` in timeline-view `local.refresh`) shows the last run of the loaded state as block 1 (id `run:runs/<file>`, opens on Details; a click on a step card shows that step, `os.refs['timeline-view'].runPick`; under it tabs Changes / Reads (`runTab`; an MCP item that sends or writes is a change, other mcp/skill/subagent/workflow and run/test/search items are reads) with source buttons All / Main agent / Subagents / MCP / Skills / Workflows (`runBy`, `SOURCES`) and a tree + tabs File / Changes / Why (`runSel`, `runSelTab`); a subagent lane starts with an `.ar-branch` line and has short cards; the uses are rows of the Details `dl`), and an Agent run block after a New version block for each run that is new in it.
- State view (the one view for the state and its changes): `ui-data.filter` (text; the editor shows only paths that have it), `filter_kind` (All = the editor; Files / Views / Functions / Network / Environment = a tree in the pane, `kindView`), `changes` (Changes), `details` (Details), `timeline_open` (Timeline button), `track_state` (Track state) and `show_empty` (the Show empty box, local.toggle-empty; false hides `{}`, `[]`, `""`, `null` with collapsed marks and no "⋯": state-core `filterLines(text, map, q, kind, {hideEmpty})` returns those ranges as `[from, to, 'empty']`). The bar: Timeline button, kind buttons, Changes and Details, filter with Show empty and Track state, collapse, save, then older / newer. local.refresh folds the other lines into "⋯ N lines" marks (`os.refs['state-view'].hide`).
- Record button (`extension.views.recorder-view`, rendered by index-view `local.init` into `<div id="recorder-view">`, fixed bottom right): one click `local.start {mode: 'audio'}`, two clicks (300 ms) video; keys Arrow Up two times (400 ms) audio, Arrow Up + Arrow Down together video, same keys or a click stop (`local.stop`); not in inputs or CodeMirror. Media (MediaRecorder, the blob, the object URL), the listeners and the select-mode frames are in `os.refs['recorder-view']`, never in the state. ui-data: `recording`, `started_at`, `selected`, `selections` [{at, path}], `result` {kind, time, size, type}, `error`. The header has `#rec-timer` (drawn every 250 ms while it records). Select mode: capture listeners stop the page's clicks; `local.select {path}` (path = view state path › css path from the view, + timeline block). `local.save` uses the `downloads` capability (declared on the artifact), else an `<a download>`. Its calls are timeline blocks only with Track state on. Holding the button 4 s calls `local.open-notes` (renders `extension.views.notes-view`, a full page, empty for now; its `local.close` unmounts it); the click after the hold does nothing (`os.refs['recorder-view'].held`). Tests fake getUserMedia/getDisplayMedia (`fakeMedia`).

## Releases
`agents.agent-oss.files` is always the files of main (every file of the repo except `state.json`, which is the state, and `gen/`, which makes it; a folder with only `.gitkeep` is `{}`). The docs live in `docs/` and in `agents.agent-oss.files.docs`.

`state.json` is made by `gen/make_state.py` (views, functions and tests; `gen/docs_part.py` writes `docs/`, `gen/pseudo.py` has the pseudo code, `gen/style_part.py` the styles). Change the generator, not `state.json`, then run `CM_DIR=<codemirror@5.65.16 npm package> python3 gen/make_state.py`. The tests need the same `CM_DIR`: `CM_DIR=... node --test tests/*.test.js`. `node gen/build.js <previous commit.json> <release.json> <out dir>` makes the next `commits/cNNNNNN` document (release.json: `request`, `session`, `explain`).

When a Claude Code session changes files:
1. Put the files of main into the state (`agents.agent-oss.files`) and run the tests.
2. Commit to main and push.
3. Record the run: run the `run-recorder` subagent (or do its steps) with `--from` the commit before the run and `--to` the new commit. Commit `runs/<session>-<run>.json`, put the files into the state again, and commit.
4. Save the new version as `commits/cNNNNNN` with `source`: `git` (commit hash), `branch` (`main`), `message`, `request` (the owner's words that asked for it), `session` (link), `explain` (`[{part, before, now}]`, in ASD-STE100: how each part worked before and how it works now).
5. An open page runs the new version at once (`loadNewerVersion`, input `{head, from}`); each view keeps its ui-data. The timeline's New version block shows the state changes between `from` and `head`, and in Details the source, `explain` side by side, and each changed file side by side.

1. The runtime reads all saved versions from the page database.
2. The newest version becomes the live state.
3. The runtime calls the function render for index-view.
4. render fills the html of a view with its ui-data and puts it into the element of the view.
5. You click a button. The button calls a function of its view.
6. The function changes the state, for example the ui-data of a view. Then the views show the new state.
7. The Save button of the state view saves the state as a new version in the page database.

## The parts
- The state is one JSON document. It holds all the data, views and functions of the page.
- The runtime is the file index.html. It loads the state and starts the first view. It has no page content.
- A view is one part of the page. A view has html, ui-data and functions. The html starts with one root element. The id of this element is the name of the view.
- A function is JavaScript code in the state. The runtime runs it and records the result.
- The code of a function starts with import lines. Each line names a thing that the function uses. The imports field of the function tells where each thing comes from.
- A version is a saved copy of the state. The page keeps all versions in its database.

## The timeline
1. Open the state view (the State button in the header). Click the Timeline button at the left of its bar. The timeline shows at the top of the page, above the header. Click the button again to hide it.
2. It shows what happened since the page opened, as blocks in a row from left to right. The first block is the last agent run (if the state has one). Then: Network (every request and the environment), index.html runs, the runtime loads the state, the page starts.
3. Each next block is one call that nothing else called, for example a click on a button.
4. Each block shows its number, the time since the page opened, the function, its time in ms and how many state changes it made.
5. What you do in the state view and in the timeline (clicks on blocks, the replay, the buttons) is not a block. Turn on Track state (in the bar of the state view) to add it as blocks too.
6. When the row of blocks scrolls, the last agent run stays at the left and the newest block stays at the right.

### A block
1. Click a block. The state view shows it, and its bottom bar names it (for example "Block 3: Run index.html"). When no block is chosen, the state view shows the last agent run.
   The state view goes to the version of the block: the version that an agent run made, or that a New version brought. For the other blocks, it is the newest version.
2. Changes (the button in the bar of the state view): the state cut down to what this block changed: green is added, yellow is updated (with the old value), red is deleted. Under it, a table says which function changed what.
   A long text, or a text of more than one line, shows as "...", as in the state view. Put the pointer on it to see its start. An updated text (and its "was "..."") shows its changes: red lines are removed, green lines are added. Click it to open the whole text in the viewer. Press Escape or × to close the viewer.
   Type in Filter paths (the filter of the state view) to see only the paths that have the text. The table shows only the paths that the filter shows.
   The buttons All, Files, Views, Functions, Network and Environment choose what shows. All shows the changes as above. Each other button shows only that kind, in its own view:
   - On the left: a tree of all of them in the state after the block (for example all the files, in their folders). A changed one has the color of its change: green added, yellow updated, red deleted. A folder that holds a change is yellow.
   - On the right: the one that you click, in tabs. The first tab is its content: File (the text of the file), View (its html and ui-data), Function (its code and its other fields), Request (a request of network) or Value (a part of environment).
   - A function also has the Pseudo code tab: its docs, then what its code does, step by step. Each line has a number. The keywords have colors: IF, ELSE and FOR EACH (the flow) are purple, CALL is blue, SET, READ, DRAW and the other actions are green, RETURN and THROW are red. A line inside a step is indented, with a guide line.
   - When the block changed it, the Changes tab shows the change. A text (a file, html, code) shows side by side: red lines are only before, green lines are only after. An object shows cut down to what changed.
   - The filter text keeps only the items whose path has it.
   - A file shows in the file viewer for its kind. The head has a badge for the kind (JS, HTML, CSS, JSON, MD, PY), the name, the language, the lines, the size, the tokens (about), Copy and Full screen.
     - Full screen: the file viewer covers the page. Click Exit full screen or push Escape to go back.
     - md: reads as a page, with the look and the theme of the md viewer of the state view. Contents on the left lists the headings: click one to go to it. The "Aa" buttons choose the theme: Reader, White, Black, Sepia, Night or Mono. The theme stays in state-view ui-data.md_theme, so the md viewer of the state view uses it too. Source shows the text.
     - json: a tree. Click an object or a list to open or close it. The first two levels are open. Find opens the parts that have the text and marks them. Open all, Close all. Source shows the text.
     - Code (js, html, css, python and more): the outline on the left (functions, classes and constants; ids, scripts and styles; selectors), each with its line. Click one to go to the line. Find marks every match: Enter goes to the next one, Shift+Enter to the one before. Wrap wraps long lines.
   - A click on "..." opens the text in the same file viewer.
3. Details (the button after Changes): what happens inside the block. The function, then each function it called, in the order they started, with their input and time.
   Each function says what it does (its docs), why it ran (a click, a watch, or the function that called it) and what it changed in the state. Click its name to see its code.
   The first blocks happen before any function runs, so they show their parts instead:
   - Run index.html: the runtime script runs. What it did, with times, the start time (os.started), the session id of the call log, the call tracker, and the functions in os.
   - Load the state: state.json downloads, the page connects to the database, reads the saved versions and parses the newest one.
   Each part says what happens and why it is needed. Click a part to open it: it shows the lines of index.html that do it (with their line numbers), then what it made:
   - Run the runtime script shows what the runtime did, with times, and the code of the runtime script.
   - Note the start time shows the browser's timings. Make a session id shows the first record of the call log. Create the call tracker counts the calls by name. Build os lists what is in os: click one to see what it is for, which functions use it, how often they ran, and its code.
   - Download state.json shows state.json. Connect to the database shows where the versions and the call log are. Read the saved versions lists the versions. Parse the newest version shows the parts of the state and their sizes.
### The buttons of the timeline
1. The arrow buttons show the block before and the next block.
2. The Replay button shows the next block every 1.6 seconds. From the last block, it starts again at the first. It goes on to the newest block. With Track state on, each move adds a block, so it stops at the block that was the newest when it started. It also stops when you click it again, or when you click a block.
3. The Reload button reloads the page, so the history starts again at block 1. The timeline opens again and replays the blocks from the first one: the last agent run, then the page start. If the state has unsaved changes, it does not reload: save them first.
4. The blocks button hides or shows the row of blocks.
5. The Flows button opens the list of saved flows. Click the play button of a flow to replay only its blocks. First enter is the page opening: its first 4 blocks (index.html, runtime, loadState, the render of index-view).
6. The timeline is part of the state view: when you close the state view, the timeline hides too.

### A new version
1. A Claude Code session changes the files of main. It commits the change, pushes it and saves a new version of the state.
2. An open page gets the new version and runs it immediately. You do not reload the page.
3. Each view keeps its ui-data. The views that were open stay open.
4. The timeline adds a New version block.
5. Changes: the differences between the version that ran before and the new version. Long texts are cut.
6. Details: where the version came from (the git commit, the request and the session), how each part worked before and how it works now, side by side, and each changed file side by side. Red lines are only in the old version. Green lines are only in the new version.

### Agent runs
1. An agent run is one request to an agent (Claude Code): from a message (of a person, the coordinator or a notification) to the next message.
2. After each run that changes the files of main, the agent records the run in runs/<session>-<run>.json:
   - scripts/run-log.js reads the session log (the .jsonl file of Claude Code). It makes the raw data: the requests, the context sizes, each tool use and the files.
   - The run-recorder subagent (.claude/agents/run-recorder.md) reads the raw data. It groups the tool uses into steps and writes why for each step, use and file. It does not copy secrets or the content of files.
   - The release puts the files of main into the state, so the run is in agents.agent-oss.files.runs.
3. The timeline shows the last run of the state as block 1, before the page start. A new version that comes with new runs gets an Agent run block after the New version block, for each new run.
4. Click an Agent run block, then Details:
   - The chips: the agent, the session, the run, the start and end time, the version that the run made, the context at the start and at the end, the cached part of the context, and whether the session was compacted.
   - Timeline (Agent run): the start card, then each step from left to right. Each step is in the lane of the agent that did it. The first lane is the main agent. A subagent is a helper agent with its own context, which the main agent started (for example run-recorder, which writes the record of the run). A subagent lane starts with a dashed line that tells what the subagent is and which steps are its own; its steps are short cards. A main agent step shows what it did (for example "read index.html", "create scripts/run-log.js"), why, its time and the context at its end. An MCP, skill, subagent or workflow use in a step is bold, with a color.
   - Click a step. Under the timeline, you see only this step: its lane, its time, its context, what it did (each item with its kind), and why. Click the step again to see the whole run.
   - Under it, two tabs. Changes: the files that the agent created, updated or deleted, and the MCP calls that sent or wrote something. Reads: what came into the context of the agent: the files that it read, the output of commands, tests and searches, and the data of MCP calls, skills and subagents.
   - The buttons show only what one source did: All, Main agent, Subagents, MCP, Skills or Workflows. Each source has its color, and each item in the tree has a chip for its source.
   - On the left, the tree: the files under Files/, in their folders, with the color of their change (green created, yellow updated, red deleted), then the other items in groups (MCP calls, Commands and tests, Searches, Subagents). On the right, the item that you click, in tabs: File (the file viewer, with the text from the version that the run made), Changes (side by side: the version before the run and the version that the run made) and Why (what, by who, in which steps, why, the size in tokens). A file that is not in the state (it is not a file of the repo) has only Why.
   - Details: what started the session, the run, the workflow, the subagents and the skills; MCP use, Skill use, Subagents and Workflow, each with how many times and why; then the context sizes.
5. Changes of an Agent run: the differences between the version before the run and the version that the run made, if this page has both versions.

### Network and environment
1. The state has two parts that the runtime fills: network and environment.
2. network has a group for each kind of request: html, scripts (our scripts), claude.ai (the scripts of the claude.ai artifact page, such as its database), api (the database calls), state, file code (code that the timeline downloads as text), packages, styles. Other requests go in other.
3. Each request has url, start (ms after the page opened), ms (download time), size (bytes), count, and parallel (what downloaded at the same time).
4. The state lists the requests that the page expects. Each has used_for (what the page uses it for) and expected: true. A request that is not in the list gets expected: false.
5. A request that this page load did not ask for (yet) has no values: count is 0.
6. environment has browser (name, version, system, screen, processor cores, memory, graphics card, connection and more), browser data (the storages and how much they use, also the claude.ai database: its versions and the call log of this page), browser api, document (title, elements, focus, fonts and more), window (sizes, scroll, origin and more), event listeners, timers, observers, connections, devices, permissions, subscriptions, background services and other.
   - event listeners: each element (or window, document) that has listeners, each event, how many, and who added them: the call that was running, or the page.
   - timers: the timeouts that wait, the intervals and the animation frames, with who added them.
   - observers: MutationObserver, ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver and PerformanceObserver, with what they watch and who added them.
   - connections: the open WebSocket, EventSource and BroadcastChannel connections.
   - devices: how many cameras, microphones and speakers, the battery, gamepads, and which device APIs the browser has.
   - permissions: the state of each permission (granted, denied or prompt).
   The runtime finds listeners, timers, observers and connections because it wraps the browser functions that add them, before other code of the page runs. Code that ran before the runtime (the scripts of claude.ai) is not in these lists.
7. Each call writes network and environment into the state when it starts and when it ends. So the Changes of a block show what the block loaded and what changed around the page. expected-state-change does not check network and environment.
8. Block 1, Network, shows every request in its group: the url, the size, the time (in the version that this page loaded, now, and the difference), what downloaded in parallel, expected and used for. Click a request to see its code. A file on another address (cdnjs, Google Fonts) runs on the page, but the browser can stop the page from downloading it as text. Then the request shows why, and a link that opens the file. Environment is next to it. A yellow value is not the same as in the version that this page loaded.
9. When you save a version, it keeps network and environment as they are. The next page load shows the difference.

### Where it comes from
1. The timeline comes from the call log of the runtime (os.calls), not from the state. If the state kept the timeline, each call would change the state again.
2. The ui-data of timeline-view keeps the chosen block (selected; null is the last agent run), whether the replay runs (playing), show_blocks, flows_open, and the saved flows (flows: each has a name and the names of its blocks). The ui-data of state-view keeps timeline_open (the Timeline button), track_state (Track state), changes and details.

## Record
The red button at the bottom right of the page records (recorder-view).
1. Click it one time to record audio (the microphone). Click it two times to record video (a screen, a window or a tab that you choose, with its sound and the microphone).
2. Or use the keys (not while you type in a field or an editor): push Arrow Up two times to record audio. Push Arrow Up and Arrow Down at the same time to record video.
3. While it records, the button is a stop button, and the header shows the kind and the time (for example "Audio 00:12").
4. While it records, you are in select mode. The element under the pointer has a red frame. Click an element to select it: the page does not get the click. A timeline block or a view part has a purple frame, and its path shows above it: the view in the state, then the elements down to it, and the block (for example "extension.views.timeline-view › #tl-strip > button.tl-step:nth-of-type(3) (block 3: Run index.html)").
5. To stop, click the button, push the same keys again, or stop the sharing of the browser.
6. The card above the button plays the recording and lists the elements that you selected, with their time. Save file saves it (webm). On claude.ai, you confirm the download. The close button forgets the recording. The recording is in the memory of the page only, not in the state.
7. The browser asks you to let the page use the microphone or the screen. If it does not let the page record, a red note above the button tells why.
8. The ui-data of recorder-view keeps: recording ("", audio or video), started_at, selected (the last path), selections (each {at, path}), result (kind, time, size, type) and error. The calls of the record button are timeline blocks only when Track state is on.
9. Hold the button for 4 seconds to open the Notes page (notes-view). It covers the page. It is empty for now. Click × to close it. When you release the button after the 4 seconds, it does not record.

## Where the parts are
- Views: extension.views.
- Shared functions: extension.functions.
- Files of the agent: agents.agent-oss.files. These are the files of main, except state.json (state.json is the state).
- These docs: agents.agent-oss.files.docs (docs/ in the repo).

## Rules
- All the data that a view shows is in the ui-data of that view.
- A function changes the state. Then the view shows the new state.
- The expected-state-change of a function tells which parts of the state it can change. If the function changes nothing, it is empty.
- After each run, the runtime updates the output, performance and errors of the function.
- When a newer version is saved in a different place, an open page shows it immediately. Each view keeps its ui-data. Unsaved edits in the state view stop this.
- To change the page, change the state and save it. Do not change index.html.

# Functions

## The fields of a function
- input: the parameters of the function, with example values. For render, the parameter is view_path.
- output: the value that the function returned in its last run. If the function returns nothing, output is empty.
- imports: where each import line of the code comes from. "index.html" is the runtime. A URL loads a script. Source code is a module. A path in the state points to source code or URLs that the state keeps one time.
- tests: the checks for the function.
- expected-state-change: the parts of the state that the function can change, and how.
- docs: a short text that tells what the function does.
- pseudo: what the code does, step by step, in short lines with keywords (SET, READ, IF, ELSE, FOR EACH, CALL, DRAW, WATCH, WAIT, RETURN, THROW). A line inside a step starts with 2 more spaces. When you change the code, change the pseudo code too.
- performance: the time of the last run, the shortest and longest time, and the number of runs. The unit is milliseconds.
- code: the function as JavaScript, with its name and its parameters.
- calls: the functions that this function calls, with their input and their last output.
- errors: the problems of the last run. The runtime writes this field.

## Example: get-state with all its fields
```json
{
  "input": { "path": "extension.views.header-view" },
  "output": { "html": "...", "ui-data": { "docs_open": false, "state_open": false }, "functions": { ... } },
  "imports": { "os": "index.html" },
  "tests": {
    "reads header-view": { "input": { "path": "extension.views.header-view" }, "expect": { "output-has": ["html", "ui-data", "functions"] } }
  },
  "expected-state-change": {},
  "docs": "Returns the JSON state: all of it, or the part at path (for example extension.views.header-view).",
  "pseudo": "READ the state at path (all the state when there is no path)\nIF nothing is at path\n  THROW \"Nothing at <path>\"\nRETURN a copy of the value",
  "performance": { "last": 0.1, "min": 0.1, "max": 0.4, "count": 3 },
  "code": "import os from 'os';\n\nasync function getState({ path }) { ... }",
  "calls": {},
  "errors": []
}
```
## How a function runs
1. A button, a key or a different function calls the function. A shared function has a path, for example extension.functions.render. A function of a view has a local name, for example local.save.
2. The runtime loads the imports. It gives each name of an import line its value.
3. The runtime runs the code with the input.
4. The runtime compares the state before and after the run.
5. The runtime checks the change against expected-state-change. A change that a called function made is not a change of the caller.
6. The runtime writes output, performance and errors.

## Imports
The code can use only what its import lines name. Each name must be in the imports field.
```js
import os from 'os';
import ctx from 'ctx';
import core from 'state-core';
import CodeMirror from 'codemirror';
```
```json
{
  "os": "index.html",
  "ctx": "index.html",
  "state-core": "extension.views.state-view.functions.local.init.imports.state-core",
  "codemirror": "extension.views.state-view.functions.local.init.imports.codemirror"
}
```
- os comes from index.html. It is the live state and the page:
- os.get(path): the live state at a path. Without a path, all of the state.
- os.call(name, input, view): calls a function.
- os.template(html, data): fills an html template with data.
- os.bind(element, view): connects the buttons that have data-call.
- os.watch(view, name): runs the function name after each call.
- os.refs: data that the state cannot keep, for example the editor.
- os.history: the saved versions. os.preview: a page that runs one view with a copy of the state.
- ctx comes from index.html. It is this call:
- ctx.call(name, input): calls a different function and records the call.
- ctx.root: the element of the view of the function.
- state-core is a module. Its source is in the state one time, in local.init of state-view. The other functions point to it.
- codemirror is the editor. Its scripts load from cdnjs. The name CodeMirror is the editor that the scripts give.

## The rules of expected-state-change
- "changes": the value must change.
- "toggles": the value must change from true to false, or from false to true.
- "input.name": the value must become the input parameter with that name.
- "may change": the value can change.
- Other values: after the run, the value must be equal to this value.
- "*": all changes are permitted.

## Tests
- before: the calls that prepare the page for the test.
- input: the input for the function.
- expect: what must be true after the run. You can check output, output-has, dom, dom-absent, state and state-changed.
- The runtime also checks the errors of the run. A test with errors fails.
- The result of each test goes into the result field of the test.

## Example: a test of local.toggle-changes
```json
{
  "turns the changes view on": {
    "before": {
      "extension.functions.render": { "view_path": "extension.views.state-view" },
      "local.filter-kind": { "kind": "all" }
    },
    "input": {},
    "expect": {
      "state": { "extension.views.state-view.ui-data.changes": true },
      "dom": ["#changes[aria-pressed=\"true\"]", "#tl-detail:not([hidden]) .st-legend, #tl-detail:not([hidden]) .tl-text"]
    }
  }
}
```
1. before renders the state view and pushes All. Then ui-data.changes is false.
2. The runtime runs local.toggle-changes with the input {}.
3. The runtime checks that ui-data.changes is true, that the Changes button is pressed, and that the pane shows the changes.

# The state view

## Open the state view
1. Click the State button in the header.
2. The state view shows the chosen block of the timeline. When no block is chosen, it is the last agent run. The editor shows the state at the version of the block.
3. The state view is the one view for the state and its changes. Its bar has, from the left: the Timeline button, the kind buttons, Changes and Details, the filter with Show empty and Track state, then Collapse all, Save, Older and Newer.

## Edit and save the state
1. Edit the JSON in the editor. You can write comments with // and /* */.
2. Push Cmd+S or Ctrl+S, or click the Save button.
3. If the JSON has small errors, the save repairs them first.
4. The border of the editor becomes green for a short time. This shows that the new version is saved.

## Filter the state
1. Type in the filter at the top of the state view.
2. The editor shows only the entries whose path has the text, with the first and last lines of the objects around them.
3. The other lines fold into "⋯ N lines". You can still edit the lines that show.
4. Click Files, Views, Functions, Network or Environment to see only that kind, as a tree: for example, Files shows the files in their folders. Click one in the tree to see it on the right. Click All to see the editor again. This works with or without text.
5. Click Changes to see only what the chosen block changed. After Older or Newer, it is what the version on the screen changed. Click Details to see what happens inside the block.
6. Clear Show empty to hide the entries with an empty value: {}, [], "" or null. They hide with no "⋯" mark.
7. Turn on Track state to add what you do in the state view and the timeline as blocks of the timeline.
8. Push Escape to clear the filter.
- Older and newer (the arrows) are at the right end of the bar.
- The version, the path and the status are in the bar at the bottom of the state view.

## Look at older versions
1. Click the left arrow button, or push the left arrow key. The state view leaves the chosen block.
2. You cannot edit an older version.
3. Click the Changes button to see only the changes of that version. Green is added, yellow is updated, red is deleted.

## Long text
- Long text, and text that has more than one line, shows as "...". Put the pointer on it to see the start of the text, in the colors of its kind (md, js, html, css or json).
- Click the "..." to open the text in the viewer. You can edit it there.
- When you close the viewer, your changes go into the editor. Then save them.

## Read and edit an md file
1. Click the "..." of an md file, for example agents.agent-oss.files.docs.how-it-works.md.
2. The file shows as a document. Click a line and edit the text there.
3. Push Enter to start a new line of the same kind: a new item, the next step, or a paragraph.
4. Push Backspace at the start of a line to remove its mark. Push it again to join the line to the line before it.
5. Click the arrow next to a heading to fold its section. Click it again to open the section.
6. Click a theme button above the document to change how it looks: Reader (the default, for long reading), White, Black, Sepia, Night or Mono. The theme stays in ui-data.md_theme.

## Try a view in the viewer
1. Click the "..." of the html of a view, for example extension.views.header-view.html.
2. The html is on the left. On the right, the view runs with a copy of the state.
3. Click a button of the view. The function of the button runs in the copy. Nothing is saved.
4. Below the view, you see the ui-data of the view. The lines that the last action changed are yellow.
5. Edit the html on the left. The view on the right starts again with the new html.

local.init.docs: Runs when the page loads, after index-view is rendered: reads header-view and renders it, then renders the record button (recorder-view).
local.init.pseudo:
CALL get-state for extension.views.header-view
IF there is no header-view: THROW
CALL render for header-view
CALL render for recorder-view (the record button)

local.init.docs: Runs after header-view is rendered: opens docs-view and state-view again when ui-data says they are open. After the Reload button of the timeline, it opens the state view with the timeline.
local.init.pseudo:
READ ui-data of header-view
IF the page reloads from the Reload button of the timeline
  SET state_open = true, and timeline_open of state-view = true
IF docs_open and docs-view is not mounted: CALL render docs-view
IF state_open and state-view is not mounted: CALL render state-view

local.open.docs-view.docs: The Docs button: renders docs-view, or closes it when it is open, and keeps ui-data.docs_open in step.
local.open.docs-view.pseudo:
SET docs_open = NOT (docs-view is mounted)
IF docs_open
  CALL render docs-view
ELSE
  CALL unmount docs-view
CALL render header-view (the button shows pressed or not)

local.open.state-view.docs: The State button: renders state-view, or closes it when it is open, and keeps ui-data.state_open in step.
local.open.state-view.pseudo:
SET state_open = NOT (state-view is mounted)
IF state_open
  CALL render state-view
ELSE
  CALL unmount state-view
CALL render header-view

local.init.docs: Runs after docs-view is rendered: lists the docs folder and shows the selected doc.
local.init.pseudo:
READ the docs folder of the agent (agents.agent-oss.files.docs)
SET docs = the names of the files in it
IF selected is not one of them: SET selected = the first doc
SET content = the text of the selected doc
DRAW the view again from its html and ui-data
BIND its buttons

local.open-doc.docs: Shows one doc of the folder.
local.open-doc.pseudo:
IF name is not in the docs folder: THROW "No doc"
SET selected = name
SET content = the text of the doc
DRAW the view again from its html and ui-data
BIND its buttons

local.init.docs: Runs after timeline-view is rendered (the state view renders it): draws the timeline now and after every call. After the Reload button, it replays the blocks from the first one.
local.init.pseudo:
IF an older timeline has a replay timer: STOP it
SET os.refs.timeline-view = a new empty memory (steps, parts, files)
WATCH timeline-view: after each call, CALL local.refresh
CALL local.refresh
IF the page reloads from the Reload button
  CALL local.select the first block (the last agent run)
  CALL local.play

local.refresh.docs: Draws the timeline from the runtime's call log: the page opening, index.html, then every call that nothing else called, as blocks in a row. What you do in the state view and the timeline is a block only when Track state is on. The last agent run stays at the left and the newest block at the right when the row scrolls. It shows only when the Timeline button of the state view is on. It keeps the chosen block for the state view, with how to draw its changes and its details. Runs after every call; after is the call that ran.
local.refresh.pseudo:
SHOW the timeline IF state-view is mounted and its timeline_open is true, ELSE HIDE it
DRAW the bar again from ui-data (buttons, flows list)
READ the call log of this page load (os.calls)
FOR EACH call
  IF another call made it: PUT it inside that call
  ELSE IF it is a call of the timeline, the state view or the record button, and Track state is off: SKIP it
  ELSE: it is a block
SET blocks =
  the last agent run of the state (runs/*.json), if there is one
  Network (requests and environment)
  Run index.html
  each top call (Load the state, Start the page, clicks, new versions)
  after a New version: an Agent run block for each new run
FOR EACH block: count its state changes
SET the chosen block = selected, or the last agent run when nothing is chosen (the newest block when there is no run)
DRAW the row of blocks (number, time, name, changes); the chosen block is on
  the last agent run stays at the left, and the newest block at the right, when the row scrolls
DRAW the position and the progress line
GIVE the state view what it needs:
  current = the chosen block, number = its place
  versionOf(block) = the version the block made or brought (the newest version for the other blocks)
  showTip(element, text, path, old text) = the preview of a long text: its first lines in the colors of its kind;
    with the old text, its changes (red lines out, green lines in), from a little before the first change
  pairFrom(before, after) = two states and the rows of what changed
  drawPair(box, kind, pair) = the changes of two states (all, or one kind as a tree)
  kindView(box, kind, state) = one kind of the state as a tree
  drawChanges(box, kind) = the state changes of the block
    ALL: the state cut down to the changes, long texts as "...", a table of who changed what
    ONE KIND (files, views, functions, network, environment):
      a tree of all of them on the left
      tabs on the right: the content (File / View / Function / Request / Value), Pseudo code, Changes
      a file shows in the file viewer (md page, json tree, code with outline)
  drawDetails(box) = what happens inside the block
    Network: the requests by group and the environment
    Agent run: the steps in lanes, the uses, what started it, the files as a tree
    a call: its parts, then each call inside it with what, why and its changes
IF playing and no timer: START a timer that CALLs local.next every 1.6 s
IF not playing and a timer runs: STOP it

local.select.docs: Chooses a block: the state view shows it (its version, its changes, its details). It stops the replay. id null chooses no block: the state view shows the last agent run.
local.select.pseudo:
SET playing = false, and leave the flow
SET selected = id (null: no block, the state view shows the last agent run)

local.next.docs: Moves delta blocks back (-1) or forward (1). The replay calls it with 1 and stops at the block that was the last when it started.
local.next.pseudo:
IF a flow is not playing: leave the flow
SET ids = the blocks of the flow, or all the blocks
SET to = the place of the chosen block (or the block that shows) + delta (not past the first or the last)
SET selected = ids[to]
IF to is the last block, or the end of the replay: SET playing = false

local.reload.docs: The Reload button: reloads the page, so the history starts again from the first block. Then the timeline opens and replays it. It stops when the state has unsaved changes.
local.reload.pseudo:
IF the state has unsaved changes: THROW "Save them first"
REMEMBER "replay after the reload" (sessionStorage, or the address)
RELOAD the page

local.toggle-blocks.docs: Hides or shows the row of blocks.

local.toggle-flows.docs: The Flows button: opens or closes the list of saved flows.

local.play-flow.docs: Plays a saved flow of ui-data.flows: its blocks, one after the other, every 1.6 seconds. Each name in the flow is the first block with that name after the block before it. First enter is the page opening: its first 4 blocks.
local.play-flow.pseudo:
FIND the flow with this name in ui-data.flows
IF there is none: THROW "No flow"
SET ids = []
FOR EACH block name of the flow
  FIND the first block with that name after the block found before
  IF found: ADD it to ids
IF ids is empty: THROW
SET the flow = { name, ids }, and the end of the replay = the last of ids
SET flows_open = false
SET selected = the first of ids
SET playing = true IF the flow has more than one block
RETURN { blocks: the number of ids }

local.play.docs: Starts or stops the replay: the next block shows every 1.6 seconds, up to the newest block. With Track state on, it stops at the block that was the newest when it started. From the last block, it starts again at the first. A paused flow goes on.
local.play.pseudo:
IF the flow ended: leave the flow
SET ids = the blocks of the flow, or all the blocks
SET playing = NOT playing
IF playing and the chosen block is the last (or none): SET selected = the first block
IF playing
  SET the end = the newest block now IF Track state is on, ELSE no end (it goes on to the newest)

local.init.docs: Runs after state-view is rendered: starts the editor at the newest version, renders the timeline (hidden until the Timeline button) and watches the state (local.refresh runs after each call).
local.init.pseudo:
READ the saved versions (os.history)
SET the memory of the view: the editor, the draft, the base text (the newest version)
SET ui-data: the version, the position, no changes, no unsaved draft
CREATE the editor (CodeMirror) with folds, colors for keys and matching brackets
WHEN you type: WAIT a moment, then CALL local.edit
WHEN you press the arrow keys (not in the editor): CALL local.step with -1 or 1
WHEN you press Cmd+S or Ctrl+S anywhere: CALL local.save
WHEN you type in Filter paths: CALL local.filter; Escape empties it
IF timeline-view is not mounted: CALL render timeline-view (hidden until the Timeline button; it keeps the blocks)
WATCH state-view: after each call, CALL local.refresh
CALL local.refresh

local.refresh.docs: Draws the view from ui-data and the state: the bar, the chosen block of the timeline (it goes to the version of the block), and what shows: the editor (draft, live state or an older version), or the pane with Details of the block, its Changes, or one kind as a tree. Runs after every call; after is the call that ran.
local.refresh.pseudo:
IF you type and local.edit did not run yet: RETURN (leave the editor alone)
IF the timeline has a newly chosen block
  the view is on the block: SET position = the version of the block (IF there is no draft)
SET the text =
  IF there is a draft and it is the newest position: the draft
  ELSE IF it is the newest version: the live state (keep the comments and the layout; change only the values)
  ELSE: the older version at position
IF the text is not the text in the editor
  SET the text in the editor, and fold again the objects that were folded
SET the editor to read only IF it shows an older version
MARK a bad line IF the JSON has an error
SHOW each long text as "..." (the pointer shows its start in the colors of its kind, a click CALLs local.open-viewer)
HIDE the lines that the filter text does not show ("... N lines")
IF show_empty is false: HIDE the entries with an empty value ({}, [], "" or null), with no mark
DRAW the buttons, the kind buttons, Show empty, Track state and the bottom bar again from ui-data
OPEN or CLOSE the viewer as viewer_path says
SET the md theme of the viewer
DRAW the chosen block in the bottom bar (IF the view is on it)
IF details, changes or a kind (not all)
  HIDE the editor and SHOW the pane
  IF details: the text of the block, then CALL drawDetails of the timeline
  ELSE IF changes and the view is on the block: CALL drawChanges of the timeline with the kind
  ELSE IF changes: CALL drawPair with the version before and the version on screen (or the draft)
  ELSE: CALL kindView with the state on screen (a tree of the kind)
  KEEP the scroll IF it shows the same thing
ELSE
  SHOW the editor and HIDE the pane

local.edit.docs: Runs as you type: keeps the unsaved draft and checks the JSON.
local.edit.pseudo:
READ the text of the editor
SET draft = the text, or null IF it is the same as the saved text
IF there is a draft: the view leaves the chosen block
SET unsaved = there is a draft
SET position = the newest (the draft is after the last version)
SET error = "", fixable = false
TRY to parse the text (JSON with comments)
IF it fails
  SET error = the message
  IF autofix repairs it: SET fixable = true

local.step.docs: Older and Newer: moves delta versions back (-1) or forward (1) in the history, and leaves the chosen block (Changes shows the changes of the version). Also runs on the arrow keys.
local.step.pseudo:
SET last = the last position (the draft counts when there is one)
SET position = position + delta, not past the first or the last
the view leaves the chosen block (Changes shows the changes of the version)

local.toggle-changes.docs: Changes: shows only what the chosen block changed (or the version on screen, after Older or Newer): added green, updated yellow, deleted red, with a table of what changed. One kind shows as a tree. It leaves Details.
local.toggle-changes.pseudo:
IF details is on: SET changes = true
ELSE: SET changes = NOT changes
SET details = false

local.toggle-details.docs: Details: shows what happens inside the chosen block of the timeline (its parts, its calls, an agent run in lanes).

local.toggle-timeline.docs: The Timeline button: shows or hides the timeline above the header. Hidden, the timeline still keeps its blocks for the state view.
local.toggle-timeline.pseudo:
SET timeline_open = NOT timeline_open
IF timeline-view is not mounted: CALL render timeline-view

local.toggle-tracking.docs: The Track state box: turns on or off that what you do in the state view and the timeline (clicks, the replay) is added as blocks of the timeline.

local.collapse-all.docs: Folds every object in the editor.
local.collapse-all.pseudo:
FOR EACH line of the editor, from the last to the first
  IF an object starts on the line: FOLD it

local.open-viewer.docs: Opens a long text in the viewer, where you can edit it. An md file shows as a document that you edit in place, with sections that fold. For html, the view runs on the right with a copy of the state: its buttons work, and its ui-data shows below it after each action.
local.open-viewer.pseudo:
READ the value at path, as it is on the screen (an older version shows its own)
SET viewer_path = path
SET the memory of the viewer: the keys, the first value, can you edit it
CREATE the editor of the viewer once
SET its mode by the kind: html, code, json, md or text
IF html
  RUN the view in the frame next to the code, with a copy of the state that has this html
  AFTER each action in the frame: SHOW the ui-data of the view and what changed
  WHEN you type: WAIT 400 ms, then RUN it again
IF md
  SHOW the text as a page that you edit in place, in the md theme
  FOR EACH line: a heading, an item, a step or a paragraph

local.filter.docs: Shows only the entries whose path has the text, with the objects around them: in the editor the other lines fold into "⋯ N lines"; the trees and the table of the changes keep only those paths. Empty text shows all.

local.close-viewer.docs: Closes the viewer; edited html or code goes into the state editor as an unsaved change.
local.close-viewer.pseudo:
IF you can edit the viewer and its text changed
  PUT the new text into the editor, in place of the old value
SET viewer_path = ""
STOP the timer of the viewer and forget it
EMPTY the frame and hide the viewer
IF the text went into the editor: CALL local.edit

local.save.docs: Saves the editor's text as a new version (fixing JSON slips first), flashes the editor border green, and renders the header from the new state. Returns the new version, what changed, and whether slips were fixed.
local.save.pseudo:
READ the text of the editor
IF it is the same as the saved text: THROW "Nothing to save"
TRY to parse the text
IF it fails: SET the text = autofix(text), parse it again, SET fixed = true
SET the ui-data of state-view in the text to the new version (version, position, no draft)
WAIT for the database to save the new version (commit n + 1)
SET the live state = the new state
SET the base text = the text; there is no draft; the view leaves the chosen block
SET the editor text IF it is not the same
SHOW a green border for 2 seconds
CALL render header-view
RETURN { version, changes (the first 50 paths), fixed }

local.init.docs: Runs after recorder-view is rendered: the record button (one click: audio, two clicks: video), the keys (Arrow Up two times: audio; Arrow Up and Arrow Down together: video), the timer in the header and the select mode.
local.init.pseudo:
IF an older init has listeners: REMOVE them
SET os.refs.recorder-view = a new memory
WHEN you hold the record button 4 s: CALL local.open-notes (the click after it does nothing)
WHEN you click the record button
  IF it records: CALL local.stop
  ELSE IF a second click comes in 300 ms: CALL local.start with video
  ELSE: CALL local.start with audio
WHEN you push Arrow Up two times in 400 ms (not in a field or an editor)
  IF it records: CALL local.stop
  ELSE: CALL local.start with audio
WHEN Arrow Up and Arrow Down are down at the same time
  IF it records: CALL local.stop
  ELSE: CALL local.start with video
WHEN it records (select mode)

render.docs: Renders a view: puts its html (with its ui-data) into the element whose id is the view's name, wires its buttons, then runs its local.init.
render.pseudo:
READ the view at view_path
IF there is no view: THROW "No view"
SET id = the last part of view_path
FIND the empty element with that id on the page
IF there is none: THROW "No element #id"
FILL the html template of the view with its ui-data (d) and e() for escape
IF the first element of the html does not have the same id: THROW
REPLACE the empty element with the new element
BIND the buttons of the element (data-call, data-input) to the functions of the view
MARK the view as mounted
IF the view has local.init
  CALL local.init of the view
